reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger, so I'll start by listing the refunds.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly, so next I'll check the orders to confirm the refunds are consistent with them before paying anyone.
Both refunds match the orders they reference and are below the order amounts, so nothing looks wrong. I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 46215, which equals its orders 27247 + 18968 = 46215 with no refunds, consistent with the ledger since no refunds reference acme. Next I'll check birch.
Acme and birch both match their order totals with no refunds, so the ledger looks consistent so far. Cobalt has both refunds, so I'll check its net balance next.
Cobalt's net of 2634 matches its orders (4653 + 33845 = 38498) minus both refunds (2289 + 33575 = 35864). The refunds are consistent with the ledger, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded. Birch's net of 65068 matches its orders (29562 + 35506) with no refunds, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's net of 2634 matches its orders minus both refunds, which I already verified against the ledger, so I'll record its payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matches the order totals minus the ledger refunds, so I'm finishing with the payout report.
